examples.en: The weather got warmer today.
Spring is here, and the breeze has gotten warmer.
I turned on the heating, and the room got warm quickly.
If you heat the soup again, it gets warm.
After drinking tea, my body warmed up.

explain: 따뜻하다와 따듯하다는 둘 다 맞는 말이에요. 보통은 따뜻하다를 더 많이 써요.
explain_en: Both 따뜻하다 and 따듯하다 are correct. 따뜻하다 is used more often.

examples.en: It got cold in the evening.
They say it'll get a lot colder starting next week.

examples.ko: 겨울이 되면 아침 공기가 많이 추워져요.
examples.en: In winter, the morning air gets very cold.

examples.ko: 해가 지면 바닷바람 때문에 훨씬 추워져요.
examples.en: After the sun sets, it gets much colder because of the sea wind.

examples.ko: 갑자기 추워졌죠? — 네, 두꺼운 옷을 입고 나왔어요.
examples.en: It suddenly got cold, didn't it? — Yes, I wore thick clothes.

explain: 아직 많이 춥지 않을 때는 “쌀쌀해지다”를 써요. 쌀쌀하다는 춥기 전의 조금 찬 느낌이에요.

dict_examples.ko: 동옥은 갑자기 추워지는 듯 전신을 움츠려 본다.
dict_examples.en: Dongok hunches her whole body as if suddenly getting cold.
dict_examples.src: 국립국어원 우리말샘 (CC BY-SA 2.0 KR) · 영어: AI 번역

explain_en: When it isn't very cold yet, use 쌀쌀해지다. 쌀쌀하다 is the slightly chilly feeling before it gets properly cold.

examples.en: I closed all the windows, so the room got hot.
Once July came, it suddenly got hot.
So many people gathered that the classroom got hot.
When it starts getting hot in spring, I check the air conditioner.
It's getting hotter and hotter, so I bought short sleeves.

explain: 덥다는 ㅂ이 바뀌는 말이에요. 덥다 → 더워요 → 더워졌어요처럼 “ㅂ”이 “워”로 바뀌어요.

dict_examples.ko: 칠월 그믐을 접어드는 여름은 본격적으로 더워졌다.
dict_examples.en: As late July set in, the summer got seriously hot.
dict_examples.src: 국립국어원 우리말샘 (CC BY-SA 2.0 KR) · 영어: AI 번역

dict_examples.ko: 날씨가 점점 더워지면서 그들도 닫쳐 두었던 문과 창을 열어젖혔다.
dict_examples.en: As the weather got hotter, they too threw open the doors and windows they had kept closed.
dict_examples.src: 국립국어원 우리말샘 (CC BY-SA 2.0 KR) · 영어: AI 번역

explain_en: 덥다 is a ㅂ-irregular word: 덥다 → 더워요 → 더워졌어요. The ㅂ turns into 워.

examples.en: After the rain, the weather cooled down.
We turned on the AC, and the office cooled down quickly.
After the sun sets, a wind blows and it gets cool.
After taking a shower, my body cooled down.
In autumn, the mornings and evenings get cool.

explain: 시원하다는 기분 좋게 서늘한 느낌이에요. 얼음처럼 차가운 것은 “차갑다”라고 해요.

phrases.example: 하고 싶은 말을 다 하니까 속이 시원해졌어요.
phrases.en: to feel relieved (after getting something off one's chest)
phrases.nuance_ko: 날씨가 아니라 답답한 마음이 풀릴 때
phrases.nuance_en: not about weather: used when a stuffy, frustrated feeling is released
phrases.en_equiv: to feel relieved (after getting something off one's chest)

explain_en: 시원하다 is a pleasantly cool feeling. Something icy cold is “차갑다”.

examples.en: I practiced every day, so my pronunciation got better.

examples.ko: 약을 먹고 푹 자니까 감기가 좋아졌어요.
examples.en: I took some medicine and slept well, and my cold got better.
After eating something tasty, I felt better.
My business is gradually getting better these days.
Shall we go on a picnic when the weather gets better? — Sure.

explain: 좋아지다와 좋아하다는 달라요. 좋아지다는 상태가 나아진다는 뜻이고, 좋아하다는 like예요.

dict_examples.en: The weather gets better.
dict_examples.src: 국립국어원 우리말샘 (CC BY-SA 2.0 KR) · 영어: AI 번역

dict_examples.en: A relationship improves.
dict_examples.src: 국립국어원 우리말샘 (CC BY-SA 2.0 KR) · 영어: AI 번역

dict_examples.ko: 끊임없이 기술 개발을 한 결과 우리 제품의 품질이 많이 좋아졌다.
dict_examples.en: As a result of constant technology development, the quality of our products has improved a lot.
dict_examples.src: 국립국어원 우리말샘 (CC BY-SA 2.0 KR) · 영어: AI 번역

dict_examples.ko: 나의 건강이 좋아진 것은 역시 꾸준한 운동 덕분이다.
dict_examples.en: My health improved, as expected, thanks to steady exercise.
dict_examples.src: 국립국어원 우리말샘 (CC BY-SA 2.0 KR) · 영어: AI 번역

explain_en: 좋아지다 and 좋아하다 are different. 좋아지다 means something gets better; 좋아하다 means to like.

examples.en: The weather got worse in the afternoon.
My eyesight got worse from staring at my phone too long.
While talking, we both ended up in a bad mood.
Since the fight, my relationship with my friend has gotten worse.

examples.ko: 요즘 잠을 못 자서 건강이 나빠졌어요.
examples.en: I haven't been sleeping lately, so my health has gotten worse.

explain: 음식 맛에는 “나빠지다”를 잘 안 써요. “맛없어졌어요”가 자연스러워요.

dict_examples.en: The situation got even worse.
dict_examples.src: 국립국어원 우리말샘 (CC BY-SA 2.0 KR) · 영어: AI 번역

dict_examples.en: Grandmother's health is getting steadily worse.
dict_examples.src: 국립국어원 우리말샘 (CC BY-SA 2.0 KR) · 영어: AI 번역

explain_en: For food, people don't really say 나빠지다. “맛없어졌어요” (it got less tasty) sounds natural.

examples.en: The teacher explained it, so the homework got easier.

examples.ko: 몇 번 해 보니까 운전이 쉬워졌어요.
examples.en: After a few tries, driving got easier.
I read every day, so reading Korean has become easier.

examples.ko: 새 앱 덕분에 예약이 훨씬 쉬워졌어요.
examples.en: Thanks to the new app, booking has become much easier.

examples.ko: 수업이 쉬워졌어요? — 아니요, 오히려 더 어려워졌어요.
examples.en: Has the class gotten easier? — No, it's actually gotten harder.

explain: 내가 일부러 쉽게 만들 때는 “쉽게 만들다”를 쓰고, 저절로 변할 때는 “쉬워지다”를 써요.

dict_examples.en: The exam questions have gotten much easier.
dict_examples.src: 국립국어원 우리말샘 (CC BY-SA 2.0 KR) · 영어: AI 번역

explain_en: When you make something easy on purpose, say “쉽게 만들다”. When it just changes by itself, say “쉬워지다”.

examples.en: Classes have gotten harder since this week.
The economy got tough, and there are fewer jobs now.

examples.ko: 비가 오면 길이 미끄러워서 운전이 어려워져요.
examples.en: When it rains, the roads get slippery and driving becomes harder.
As prices went up, grocery shopping became harder.

examples.ko: 한국어 문법이 갈수록 어려워지는 것 같아요.
examples.en: Korean grammar seems to be getting harder and harder.

explain: “형편이 어려워지다”는 돈이 부족해졌다는 뜻이에요. 돈 이야기를 조심스럽게 말할 때 쓰는 표현이에요.
explain_en: “형편이 어려워지다” means money has become tight. It's a careful, indirect way to talk about money problems.

examples.en: Our home internet got faster.
I switched to a new phone, and everything got faster.
I practiced every day, so my running speed got faster.

examples.ko: 버스 전용 차로가 생겨서 출근길이 빨라졌어요.
examples.en: A bus-only lane opened, so my commute got faster.

examples.ko: 요즘 택배가 많이 빨라졌어요. — 맞아요, 다음 날 와요.
examples.en: Deliveries have gotten much faster lately. — True, they arrive the next day.

explain: 빠르다는 ‘르’가 ‘ㄹ라’로 바뀌어요. 그래서 빨라요, 빨라졌어요가 돼요. ‘빠라요’나 ‘빠라졌어요’는 틀려요.
explain_en: 빠르다 is a 르 verb: the 르 turns into ㄹ라, so you get 빨라요 and 빨라졌어요. ‘빠라요’ and ‘빠라졌어요’ are wrong.

examples.en: My computer has gotten slow.
Now that I'm older, I walk more slowly.
My phone is old, so it has gotten very slow lately.

examples.ko: 눈이 많이 와서 버스 속도가 느려졌어요.
examples.en: It snowed a lot, so the bus slowed down.

examples.ko: 게임이 갑자기 느려졌어요. — 앱을 껐다가 다시 켜 보세요.
examples.en: The game suddenly got slow. — Try closing the app and opening it again.

explain: ‘느리다’(slow)와 ‘늦다’(late)는 달라요. 속도가 낮아지면 ‘느려지다’, 시간이 뒤로 가면 ‘늦어지다’를 써요. 약속이 늦어졌어요.

dict_examples.ko: 시간이 지나면서 일꾼들의 움직임이 점점 느려졌다.
dict_examples.en: As time passed, the workers' movements gradually slowed.
dict_examples.src: 국립국어원 우리말샘 (CC BY-SA 2.0 KR) · 영어: AI 번역

dict_examples.ko: 성모 병원 앞을 지날 때는 나도 모르게 걸음이 느려졌다.
dict_examples.en: When passing in front of St. Mary's Hospital, my steps slowed without my realizing it.
dict_examples.src: 국립국어원 우리말샘 (CC BY-SA 2.0 KR) · 영어: AI 번역

dict_examples.ko: 길이 험해졌고 경사도 있었으므로 형의 휠체어는 속도가 조금씩 느려졌다.
dict_examples.en: Because the road became rough and had a slope, my brother's wheelchair gradually slowed down.
dict_examples.src: 국립국어원 우리말샘 (CC BY-SA 2.0 KR) · 영어: AI 번역

explain_en: 느리다 (slow) and 늦다 (late) are different. Speed dropping is 느려지다. Something moving later in time is 늦어지다: 약속이 늦어졌어요 (the appointment got pushed back).

examples.en: I practiced a lot, so my voice got louder too.
I turned up the volume, and the sound got louder.

examples.ko: 광고가 나오니까 TV 소리가 갑자기 커졌어요.
examples.en: When the ad came on, the TV suddenly got louder.

examples.ko: 장사가 잘돼서 가게가 두 배로 커졌어요.
examples.en: Business went well, so the shop became twice as big.

examples.ko: 사진을 두 손가락으로 벌리면 글자가 커져요.
examples.en: If you spread two fingers on the photo, the letters get bigger.

explain: 크다는 ‘ㅡ’가 빠져요. 그래서 커요, 커졌어요가 돼요. 쓰다 → 써요, 예쁘다 → 예뻐요도 같은 모양이에요.

phrases.example: 일이 커지기 전에 먼저 사과하는 게 좋아요.
phrases.en: for things to escalate; for a problem to get out of hand
phrases.nuance_ko: 크기가 아니라 문제나 사건이 심각해질 때
phrases.nuance_en: not about size: used when a problem or incident becomes serious
phrases.en_equiv: for things to escalate; for a problem to get out of hand

dict_examples.en: The scale grows.
dict_examples.src: 국립국어원 우리말샘 (CC BY-SA 2.0 KR) · 영어: AI 번역

dict_examples.en: A matter gets blown up.
dict_examples.src: 국립국어원 우리말샘 (CC BY-SA 2.0 KR) · 영어: AI 번역

dict_examples.en: A hole gets bigger the more you carve it.
dict_examples.src: 국립국어원 우리말샘 (CC BY-SA 2.0 KR) · 영어: AI 번역

dict_examples.en: The startled child's eyes grew wider and wider.
dict_examples.src: 국립국어원 우리말샘 (CC BY-SA 2.0 KR) · 영어: AI 번역

explain_en: 크다 drops its ㅡ before 어, so you get 커요 and 커졌어요. 쓰다 → 써요 and 예쁘다 → 예뻐요 work the same way.

examples.en: The pants I bought last spring have gotten too small.
I washed my sweater in hot water, and it shrank.
I ran it in the washing machine, and the T-shirt shrank.

examples.ko: 비행기가 높이 올라가서 집들이 점점 작아져요.
examples.en: The plane climbs higher, and the houses get smaller and smaller.

examples.ko: 발표할 때 목소리가 자꾸 작아져요. — 자신 있게 말해 보세요.
examples.en: When I present, my voice keeps getting quieter. — Try speaking with confidence.

explain: 아이가 자라서 옷이 안 맞으면 “옷이 작아졌어요”라고 해요. 옷이 줄지 않았어도 쓸 수 있어요.

phrases.example: 잘하는 친구들 앞에서는 저도 모르게 작아져요.
phrases.en: to feel small; to lose confidence (in front of someone)
phrases.nuance_en: not about size: used when your confidence shrinks
phrases.en_equiv: to feel small; to lose confidence (in front of someone)

dict_examples.ko: 내가 들어가자 두 사람의 목소리는 갑자기 작아졌다.
dict_examples.en: When I walked in, the two people's voices suddenly dropped.
dict_examples.src: 국립국어원 우리말샘 (CC BY-SA 2.0 KR) · 영어: AI 번역

dict_examples.ko: 그들은 점점 작아져 가는 기차를 향해 하염없이 손을 흔들고 있다.
dict_examples.en: They keep waving endlessly at the train growing smaller and smaller.
dict_examples.src: 국립국어원 우리말샘 (CC BY-SA 2.0 KR) · 영어: AI 번역

explain_en: When a child grows and the clothes no longer fit, you say 옷이 작아졌어요. It works even if the clothes did not shrink.

en: to increase in number or amount

examples.en: It's vacation, so there are more people at the library.
There are a lot more foreign tourists these days.
In winter there are more people with colds.
A baby was born, so there is more housework now.

examples.ko: 요즘 길에 전기차가 많아졌어요. — 맞아요, 조용해서 신기해요.
examples.en: There are many more electric cars on the road these days. — True, they’re so quiet, it’s amazing.

explain: ‘실력’은 ‘많아지다’ 말고 ‘늘다’를 써요. 한국어 실력이 늘었어요. “실력이 많아졌어요”는 어색해요.

dict_examples.ko: 나이가 많아져 힘든 일을 할 수가 없다.
dict_examples.en: I've gotten older and can't do hard work.
dict_examples.src: 국립국어원 우리말샘 (CC BY-SA 2.0 KR) · 영어: AI 번역

dict_examples.en: As the river became clean, there came to be more fish in it.
dict_examples.src: 국립국어원 우리말샘 (CC BY-SA 2.0 KR) · 영어: AI 번역

dict_examples.en: There are now more people exercising in the park.
dict_examples.src: 국립국어원 우리말샘 (CC BY-SA 2.0 KR) · 영어: AI 번역

dict_examples.en: As graduation time comes around, I've gotten more worries.
dict_examples.src: 국립국어원 우리말샘 (CC BY-SA 2.0 KR) · 영어: AI 번역

explain_en: For skill, use 늘다, not 많아지다. 한국어 실력이 늘었어요. “실력이 많아졌어요” sounds odd.

en: to decrease in number or amount

examples.en: It rained, so there were fewer people in the park.
I changed jobs, and my pay went down a bit.
My work decreased, so my income got smaller.

examples.ko: 아이가 크면서 같이 노는 시간이 적어졌어요.
examples.en: As the child grew up, the time we play together got shorter.

examples.ko: 올해는 눈이 오는 날이 적어졌어요. — 맞아요, 겨울이 따뜻해요.
examples.en: There are fewer snowy days this year. — True, the winter is warm.

explain: ‘적다’(few)와 ‘작다’(small)는 달라요. 수나 양이 줄면 ‘적어지다’, 크기가 줄면 ‘작아지다’를 써요.

dict_examples.en: Income decreases.
dict_examples.src: 국립국어원 우리말샘 (CC BY-SA 2.0 KR) · 영어: AI 번역

explain_en: 적다 (few, little) and 작다 (small) are different. Fewer in number or amount is 적어지다. Smaller in size is 작아지다.

examples.en: The students left, so the classroom got quiet.
The baby fell asleep, and the house went quiet.

examples.ko: 밤 열 시가 되면 우리 동네는 조용해져요.
examples.en: At ten at night, my neighborhood gets quiet.
The meeting started, and the office went quiet.

examples.ko: 친구가 갑자기 조용해졌어요. 무슨 일 있어요? — 시험을 못 봐서 그래요.
examples.en: My friend suddenly went quiet. Is something wrong? — He did badly on the exam.

explain: 도서관에서는 “조용히 해 주세요”라고 말해요. ‘조용해지다’는 시끄럽던 곳이나 사람이 바뀌었다는 뜻이에요.

phrases.example: 선생님이 들어오시자 교실이 쥐 죽은 듯이 조용해졌어요.
phrases.nuance_ko: 갑자기 아무 소리도 안 날 만큼 조용해질 때
phrases.nuance_en: used when it suddenly gets so quiet that no sound can be heard

explain_en: In a library you say 조용히 해 주세요 (“please be quiet”). 조용해지다 means a noisy place or person has become quiet.
